ceiling_directive: Extend the growing-event-curve coverage result to the published Choi--Yuan approximate-rank class by incorporating the M^R bias and deriving simultaneous nonlinear-remainder and feasible-score bounds from its primitive conditions.
improvement_directive: Derive uniform high-probability bounds for both the exact block remainders and r_n^{score} from primitive panel dimensions and Choi--Yuan ratios, so the proposed band is actually honest over a stated growing-curve class. Then compute the balanced rank-one second-order remainder and construct the common-subclass counterarray needed to identify the attainable envelope.
critique: The note does not prove feasible uniform coverage over either event-transfer class: coverage remains conditional on remainder-event and score-stability probabilities for which no class-uniform rate is established. The Choi--Yuan remainder input applies only blockwise in an i.i.d. homoskedastic source submodel, and its displayed union bound is expressly allowed not to vanish, while the feasible loading and leave-one-cell-out imputation errors receive only deterministic contamination inequalities. Consequently, the influence representation outside that source event is largely an exact definition of the residual, and the multiplier theorem is a generic transfer result rather than a completed panel inference theorem. The claimed weakest primitive envelope, its necessity counterarray, and even the early-kill second-order calculation are all left open in oeq:attainable-remainder-frontier, so the delivered result is a specialized inference scaffold rather than the advertised sharp event-curve frontier.
